knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to build the rate from billable hours, so that the costs and income come from work that can be billed. Dividing by all paid hours, or using the lowest directory offer, does not do this.
The lesson says travel, set-up and pack-down do not shrink with a small job, so a minimum charge covers that time for a single chair or rug.

The lesson says to convert the rate into time per room and per item, then check the price against the minutes the room takes. A directory average copied exactly or a friend's rate is not a check of your own times.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, visits, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
